answer: Behavioral Fingerprint Clustering. Each agent’s action history is embedded and periodically clustered; identities whose trajectories fall within a tight shared delta across independent tasks are flagged as one operator. Enforcement is retroactive devaluation: flagged clusters lose accrued rewards and reputation weight. To survive, an attacker must make each duplicate behave distinctly enough to defeat clustering—costing ongoing task-specific divergence work per identity, not a one-time fee. Like separating river branches by pigment, separation is statistical, not declared.
